contextNote: Rembrandt's print oeuvre is among the most documented and most frequently faked in Western art history. The catalogue raisonné (White and Boon 1969, refined by Hinterding) records approximately 290 accepted prints. The principal challenge is NOT identifying whether a work depicts a Rembrandt composition but whether a given impression is a lifetime impression, a contemporary impression from his circle, an 18th-19th century restrike, or a later facsimile. State identification is critical — early vs late state can be 10-100x value differential. No impression of significant value should proceed to auction without physical specialist examination.

criticalAuthenticationMarkers.authenticIndicator: Clean, well-defined plate mark. Dimensions match catalogue record.
criticalAuthenticationMarkers.reprintIndicator: Absent plate mark = photomechanical. Dimensions inconsistent = different plate.

criticalAuthenticationMarkers.authenticIndicator: Laid paper with chain lines. Warm aged cream/ivory tone. 17th century watermarks.
criticalAuthenticationMarkers.reprintIndicator: Machine-smooth paper (post-1850 restrike). Bright white or uniformly yellowed.

criticalAuthenticationMarkers.authenticIndicator: Warm brownish-black ink. Slight plate tone from hand-wiped surface.
criticalAuthenticationMarkers.reprintIndicator: Cool blue-black more typical of later periods. Perfectly clean plate.

criticalAuthenticationMarkers.authenticIndicator: Rich velvety-edged dark lines in drypoint passages — early impression indicator.
criticalAuthenticationMarkers.reprintIndicator: Clean thin lines in drypoint passages — worn or re-etched plate.

criticalAuthenticationMarkers.authenticIndicator: Recognized collector stamps from major historical collections (Lugt identifiable).
criticalAuthenticationMarkers.reprintIndicator: Absence does not disprove authenticity but presence is strong positive signal.

distinguishingFeatures: Heavy plate wear in line quality
Cooler bluer ink than 17th century impressions
Some reworked passages by other hands
knownForgeriesAndFacsimiles.valuationImpact: Fraction of lifetime impression value — typically 2-10%

distinguishingFeatures: Line quality differs subtly — typically more uniform
Plate mark dimensions rarely match catalogue exactly

valuationSensitivities.impact: Lifetime vs 18th century restrike vs 19th century restrike: approx 100:10:1
Early vs late state: 5-50x differential for multi-state works

humanEscalationTriggers: Any lifetime impression claim requires physical specialist examination
State identification requires examination of drypoint burr and plate tone
Watermark identification requires transmitted light examination
Any impression estimated above £5,000 should be reviewed by Old Master prints specialist
